Market Intelligence Briefing
subheadings: 🇺🇸 United States Mixed hold / hawkish tilt
🇪🇺 European Union Bullish ECB on hold / earnings-led
🇨🇳 China Mixed targeted easing / weak demand
🇯🇵 Japan Bullish gradual hikes / fiscal push
🇦🇺 Australia Mixed hawkish hold / strong AUD
🇵🇱 Poland Bullish easing ahead / solid growth
🔬 US–Asia Semis — SOXX / ASML / TSMC Bullish
🧮 Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
Guidance and balance sheets beat the beat
🔍 Underowned Themes — Attention and Exposure Gaps
Rare earths above the price floor
US refiners in a crude glut
Dollar firm, duration bid, cracks in private credit
🔮 Anticipatory Positioning — Markets Pricing In Future Events
$NVDA — guidance reset into Feb. 25 earnings Bullish
$OXY — balance-sheet repair meets an oil premium Bullish
Raspberry Pi / RPI — meme rally on edge AI
DHT Holdings / DHT — tanker rates at records
Tesla / TSLA — the retail favourite under pressure
Robinhood / HOOD — pre-IPO access as the next craze
body: Friday, February 20 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information cutoff: 2026-02-20 00:00 UTC. Market figures use completed observations before this date.

Macro Stance: The January FOMC minutes showed no rush to restart rate cuts and even raised the possibility of hikes The New York Times [Feb 18]. The data justify that patience: weekly jobless claims dropped by the most since November to 206,000 Bloomberg.com [Feb 19], and January payrolls rose 130,000 with unemployment down to 4.3% CNBC [Feb 11]. Growth is holding, disinflation is slow, and the Fed is firmly on hold.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.47% and the 10Y at 4.08%, leaving the 10Y−2Y spread at 61 bps; over 20 observations the 2Y fell 13 bps and the 10Y 18 bps, a bull flattening (both down, 10Y down more), with the curve positively sloped and approaching its long-run average (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-19). Beneath the index, the S&P 500 lost 1.15% over five sessions to 6,861.89 as the VIX rose to 20.23 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19).

New / Most Important: Geopolitics is the swing factor: Trump set a '10, 15 days' deadline for an Iran deal and Tehran warned of a 'crisis' Al Jazeera [Feb 19]. The next macro test is Friday's inflation report Investopedia [Feb 18]; after hawkish minutes, a firm print would push the first cut further out and keep the dollar bid.

Playbook ✓: Keep index exposure neutral and rotate: overweight energy and industrials, underweight application software and alternative managers, and hold VIX calls near 20. Add duration only on a soft inflation print with the 10Y below 4.08%; cut it if the 2Y climbs back toward 3.60%, its level 20 observations ago (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-19). A US–Iran deal plus benign inflation would flip us to adding growth beta.

Macro Stance: European leadership is earnings-driven: the STOXX 600 closed at a record high on an earnings boost while ECB leadership moved into focus Reuters [Feb 18]. Policy is a non-event for now, so we stay constructive on European equities relative to the US.

Activity & Inflation: Euro-zone inflation fell to 1.7% in January Financial Times [Feb 04], under target, which keeps the ECB comfortable on hold. The STOXX 600 gained 2.71% over 20 sessions to 625.33 against a 0.20% loss for the S&P 500, while the DAX added only 0.75% and the FTSE 100 4.70% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19): the rally favours banks, energy and defence-heavy indices over German cyclicals.

New / Most Important: Lagarde told the WSJ her baseline is to finish her ECB term WSJ [Feb 19], which damps the succession noise. EUR/USD slipped 0.73% over five sessions to 1.1789 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19), a move driven more by the firmer dollar and Iran risk than by Frankfurt.

Playbook ✓: Stay overweight the STOXX 600 versus the S&P 500, favouring banks, industrials and defence over autos, and hedge part of the euro exposure into the Iran deadline. Cut to neutral if the earnings-beat rate fades as reporting season ends, or if the succession debate turns into a question about ECB independence.

Macro Stance: China enters the post-holiday stretch with factories stabilising and households still cautious. Xi has put domestic demand and tech independence at the top of the 2026 agenda Caixin Global [Feb 17], but transmission to spending is slow. Our view is Mixed: policy is supportive at the margin and Hong Kong has held up, yet credit demand and property argue against a durable reflation call.

PMIs & Activity: The latest official manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.3 in January Reuters [Jan 30], still in contraction. Prices are improving from a low base: factory deflation eased more than forecast at the start of the year Bloomberg.com [Feb 10]. The feed carries no fresh retail-sales print, so the Lunar New Year services season is the first real test of whether the consumption tilt is working; strong post-holiday spending data would confirm it.

Credit Impulse: January new loans jumped but missed forecasts as weak demand persists Reuters [Feb 13]. The feed carries no fresh total social financing print, so we read the credit impulse as flat at best: the seasonal January surge came in below expectations. Confirmation of a turn would need household mortgage demand to recover, which the property data do not yet show.

Property: New-home prices extended their decline in January as weak demand hounds the sector Reuters [Feb 12]. Until buyers return, any stabilisation rests on policy-driven balance-sheet repair rather than demand. We need consecutive months of slower declines in new-home prices before calling a floor; until then, avoid developers and the banks most exposed to them.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Xi's agenda points fiscal support toward consumption and technology rather than another infrastructure push Caixin Global [Feb 17]. The bigger near-term swing is Washington: Trump paused China tech bans ahead of a summit with Xi Reuters [Feb 12], lowering the risk of fresh export-control shocks into the meeting. Any US tariff relief would be a second, binary upside input for exporters.

Markets & Flows: Mainland markets were shut for the holiday: the Shanghai Composite last closed at 4,082.07, down 0.48% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), and the Hang Seng at 26,705.94, up 0.53% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16). In New York, ASHR gained 0.44% over 20 sessions to 33.88 while KWEB fell 7.95% to 32.75, and USD/CNY eased 0.80% to 6.9080 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19), a steadily firmer yuan that eases outflow pressure.

New / Most Important: The weak link is platform internet: Meituan warned of a US$3.5 billion loss amid an intense food-delivery price war South China Morning Post [Feb 13], which helps explain why KWEB lagged A-shares by a wide margin. Until subsidy competition ends, China upside sits in hardware, AI and state-backed heavyweights rather than consumer platforms.

Playbook ✓: Prefer ASHR and Hong Kong index heavyweights over KWEB; keep consumer platforms underweight until delivery subsidies fade. Add to A-shares if post-holiday spending and February credit beat, and fade any rally if new-home prices keep falling. ⚠ Divergence: industry looks firmer than households — the private PMI showed factory expansion accelerating Reuters [Feb 01], and Japan's January exports hit an over three-year high on soaring shipments to China CNBC [Feb 17].

Macro Stance: Japan combines a market-friendly government with improving trade. PM Takaichi ditched austerity and reassured markets with a fiscal pledge Reuters [Feb 19]. Core inflation slowed to a two-year low Reuters [Feb 19], complicating hike timing, yet a Reuters poll still sees the BOJ at 1% by end-June Reuters [Feb 19].

Activity & Currency: January exports surged nearly 17%, an over three-year high, as shipments to China soared CNBC [Feb 17]. The Nikkei 225 closed at 57,467.83, up 8.89% over 20 sessions, while USD/JPY rose 1.01% in the prior session to 154.69 but is down 2.37% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19).

Playbook ✓: Own Japanese exporters and chip-equipment names, currency-hedged while USD/JPY trades near 154.69 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). Watch the BOJ board nominations, which Reuters reports include reflationists Reuters [Feb 19]: a dovish slate weakens the yen further and favours exporters, while a hawkish surprise is the signal to lift the hedge and add banks.

Macro Stance: The RBA hiked in February and now says there is no set path for future rates Reuters [Feb 16]. Unemployment held at 4.1%, keeping talk of another rise alive ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation [Feb 18]. A hawkish central bank meeting a stretched household sector makes the balance Mixed: strong currency, slowing domestic demand.

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD closed at 0.7044, up 4.28% over 20 sessions though down 1.14% over five, and the ASX 200 rose 3.45% over 20 sessions to 9,086.2 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). UniSuper called the local currency undervalued and is increasing its hedging Reuters [Feb 19], a structural bid from the superannuation pool.

Playbook ✓: Buy AUD/USD on dips while the RBA stays hawkish, and keep ASX exposure neutral with banks preferred over discretionary retail. Upgrade equities if the next CPI print allows the RBA to pause; cut AUD longs if an Iran escalation triggers a global risk-off.

Monetary & Activity: January CPI ran at 2.2% y/y StockWatch.pl [Feb 13] — at the NBP target but above forecasts, with economists weighing the odds of a March cut (Money.pl: 'Inflacja w celu, ale powyżej prognoz') Money.pl [Feb 13]. Aggregate growth is strong: Q4 GDP accelerated to 4% Bankier.pl [Feb 12]. The labour market is the soft spot, with wages growing at the slowest pace in five years and employment falling sharply in January (Bankier: 'Płace rosły najwolniej od 5 lat') Bankier.pl [Feb 19].

FX & Markets: The zloty is soft against a firmer dollar: USD/PLN rose 0.54% in the prior session to 3.5750, while EUR/PLN held at 4.2139, up 0.10% over 20 sessions. EPOL is up 4.15% over 20 sessions at 37.65 and the WIG20TR tracker 1.61% at 67.50. Orlen (PKN) jumped 3.05% to 111.50 and Pekao (PEO) 1.80% to 232.20, while KGHM (KGH) fell 7.26% over five sessions to 299.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19).

Companies: Orlen's refining gains offset an impairment hit, lifting the shares Reuters [Feb 19]. Pekao topped profit estimates on higher fee income Reuters [Feb 19], evidence that Polish lenders can grow fees as rate cuts approach and net interest margins compress.

Security & New Development: The EU approved €44 billion in SAFE defence loans for Poland Notes From Poland [Feb 17], a multi-year order flow for domestic defence, ammunition and infrastructure suppliers that supports capex well beyond the rate cycle.

Playbook ✓: Own Polish banks (PEO, PKO) and Orlen into a likely March cut; Pekao's fee-led beat shows lenders can offset margin compression. Receive Polish rates rather than buy the zloty while the dollar is firm, and avoid KGHM until silver stabilises; a February CPI rebound that pushes the cut out changes the call. ⚠ Divergence: January industrial production fell (Money.pl: 'Produkcja przemysłowa w Polsce w dół') Money.pl [Feb 19] and wage growth hit a five-year low Bankier.pl [Feb 19] even as GDP accelerated.

Narrative: Consensus still frames AI as a tech tailwind; the tape treats it as a threat to software margins, with the AI scare trade spreading from software to real estate Reuters [Feb 13]. XLK fell 2.50% over 20 sessions to 140.21 and Microsoft 10.28% to 398.46 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19).

Reported: EPAM plunged 20% on a tepid 2026 outlook despite an earnings beat Barron's [Feb 19], the template for IT services and seat-based software this season: a beat is necessary but not sufficient, and guidance decides the move.

EPS Upside Watch: Upside sits with tools that monetise AI build-outs rather than compete with AI agents: chip-design software, security platforms and data infrastructure. Microsoft's slide leaves little upside priced into its next cloud print, making it the large-cap rebound candidate.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The hardware layer is being paid while the application layer is sold: SMH is up 2.06% over 20 sessions as XLK falls (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). If AI agents cannibalise seat-based software, the right hedge for semis longs is short application software, not short the Nasdaq 100.

Narrative: Communication services split between AI spenders and ad-dependent platforms. XLC is up only 0.44% over 20 sessions, with META up 5.19% and GOOGL down 7.77% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). Meta's multiyear deal to buy millions of Nvidia chips Reuters [Feb 17] shows the capex race is not slowing.

Reported: Pinterest sank nearly 17% as tariffs hit earnings CNBC [Feb 13], a warning that smaller ad platforms feel tariff-squeezed merchant budgets first. Netflix is down 9.79% over 20 sessions at 77.00 and Disney 6.35% at 106.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19), with no fresh print to reset sentiment.

EPS Upside Watch: Meta's scale lets it monetise AI through ad targeting faster than peers, so it is the cleanest upside candidate. Netflix's derating sets a lower bar for its next print if engagement holds.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Capex is turning this sector into a credit story: multiyear chip commitments tie XLC multiples to bond-market appetite for AI spending, so wider tech credit spreads would hit these names before any earnings miss.

Narrative: Financials have shifted from rate beneficiaries to private-credit risk carriers. Blue Owl halted redemptions at one of its funds, deepening a selloff in private-equity shares Reuters [Feb 19]. XLF fell 2.45% over 20 sessions to 52.15 and Goldman Sachs 3.82% to 916.65 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19).

Reported: US bank prints fell outside the window, so price action was the report card: JPMorgan is up 1.99% over 20 sessions at 308.05 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19), separating fortress balance sheets from fee-driven alternative managers.

EPS Upside Watch: Balance-sheet lenders gain share: Bank of America is committing $25 billion of its own cash to private credit deals Bloomberg.com [Feb 19]. Large banks can underwrite the assets that retail-fed vehicles must sell.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The stress is liquidity, not yet losses: Blue Owl unloaded $1.4 billion in assets before restricting withdrawals WSJ [Feb 19]. If loan sales clear near par, private-credit marks are holding; the real risk is a run on semi-liquid retail vehicles that forces sales across managers.

Narrative: Energy is both the geopolitical hedge and the earnings leader: XLE rose 13.19% over 20 sessions to 55.18, with Brent at 71.66 and WTI at 66.43, up 9.84% and 9.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). Oil settled up 4% on Iran–US tensions as Russia–Ukraine talks ended without a breakthrough Reuters [Feb 18].

Reported: Occidental jumped as a $5.8 billion debt cut and dividend hike impressed investors 24/7 Wall St. [Feb 19], rewarding balance-sheet repair over volume growth. Exxon is up 12.99% over 20 sessions at 150.97 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19).

EPS Upside Watch: Refiners and integrated majors with downstream exposure: the crude glut is a boon for US refiners as fuel demand stays firm Bloomberg.com [Feb 11]. Upstream revisions follow Brent, well above its 65.24 level of 20 sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Gas is the outlier: Henry Hub collapsed 38.54% over 20 sessions to 3.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). The energy rally is a crude risk-premium trade, not a broad commodity upcycle, so gas-weighted producers are no substitute for oil exposure.

Narrative: Physical capex is the leadership theme: XLI gained 6.00% over 20 sessions to 176.34 and Caterpillar 17.84% to 760.53 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). Data-centre, grid and defence orders sit outside the AI-disruption debate.

Reported: Deere boosted its outlook and sees construction and small-agriculture demand recovering WSJ [Feb 19], extending the capex theme beyond data centres. GE gained 6.70% over five sessions to 334.74 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19) as aerospace demand stays firm.

EPS Upside Watch: Aerospace: Vietnamese airlines signed $30 billion of deals for 90 Boeing jets Reuters [Feb 18], and engine makers capture aftermarket revenue for decades. GE Aerospace and engine suppliers have the clearest path to estimate upgrades.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Boeing itself is down 6.54% over 20 sessions at 233.71 despite those orders (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19): orders are not the constraint, delivery execution is, so own the supply chain over the airframer.

Narrative: Discretionary is dragged by two megacaps: XLY fell 4.25% over 20 sessions to 116.24, Amazon 11.43% to 204.86 and Tesla 4.57% to 411.71 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). Amazon only just snapped its worst losing streak since 2006 Barron's [Feb 18] as investors question the payback on its AI capex.

Reported: DoorDash jumped as delivery demand fuelled its growth forecast Reuters [Feb 19]: this season rewards top-line acceleration over margins. Nike is up 5.23% over five sessions at 65.61 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19) as investors hunt turnarounds.

EPS Upside Watch: Platforms with operating leverage to volumes — delivery, travel — are better set up than goods retailers; housing-linked names such as Home Depot, down 1.58% over 20 sessions at 378.58 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19), need turnover to recover first.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Equal-weight retail tells a different story: XRT is up 11% 24/7 Wall St. [Feb 18] while cap-weighted XLY is down. The consumer is not the problem — two megacaps are — so equal-weight retail is the better vehicle than the sector ETF.

Narrative: Staples are the rotation trade of the year: XLP is up 6.34% over 20 sessions at 87.67 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). The move is about defensiveness and cash-flow visibility versus AI risk, not an earnings upgrade cycle.

Reported: Walmart's new CEO began with a cautious outlook after another quarter of steady sales Reuters [Feb 19]; WMT fell 1.38% in the prior session to 124.87 and Costco 0.83% to 987.82 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). Beats are being met with guidance scepticism.

EPS Upside Watch: Household and personal care with pricing power and portfolio action have more upside than volume-dependent packaged food, where we see less pricing power left. Prefer self-help restructuring stories to grocery-aisle volume plays.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Staples rallied 6.34% over 20 sessions while Walmart fell on its guidance (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19): the sector is priced for safety, not growth. Iran de-escalation or a benign inflation print that revives risk appetite would hit the most crowded defensives first, so prefer single names with self-help over XLP itself.

Narrative: Healthcare is a stock picker's market: XLV is down 0.63% over 20 sessions at 157.26, with UnitedHealth down 16.63% and Eli Lilly 5.13% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). Big Pharma looks financially unfazed by the White House drug-price deals Axios [Feb 19], which removes one overhang for large-cap pharma.

Reported: Medtronic's unchanged annual outlook clouded upbeat quarterly results Reuters [Feb 17], and the shares fell: as elsewhere, guidance outranks the beat. Devices are being priced for steady, not accelerating, growth.

EPS Upside Watch: UnitedHealth gained 3.95% over five sessions to 289.93 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19); after a 16.63% slide over 20 sessions, low expectations make managed care the likeliest source of positive revisions if medical-cost trends stabilise.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Pricing risk has faded faster than consensus assumed: pharma's resilience to the deals argues for owning large-cap pharma as a defensive alternative to crowded staples rather than paying up for XLP.

Narrative: Materials are a gold-and-copper story: gold front-month closed at 4,997.40, up 3.31% over 20 sessions, silver fell 15.88% to 77.57 and copper was flat at 5.73 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). XLB rose 7.29% over 20 sessions to 52.83, with copper's role in data-centre and grid capex supporting the producers.

Reported: Rio Tinto's earnings were flat as iron ore weakened and copper cushioned the blow Reuters [Feb 19]. Freeport is up 3.28% over 20 sessions at 62.57 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19): the market rewards copper growth over bulk commodities.

EPS Upside Watch: Gold miners: gold bounced back above $5,000 on safe-haven demand Yahoo Finance UK [Feb 19], and Newmont is up 5.46% over 20 sessions at 125.40 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). At these prices, margin upgrades are mechanical unless costs surprise.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Silver is decoupling from gold: it fell 7.39% over five sessions while gold slipped only 1.98% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). Own gold miners and copper producers, not silver, until the industrial bid for silver stabilises.

Narrative: Lower rates are helping at the margin: XLRE is up 3.97% over 20 sessions at 43.20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19), and US mortgage rates fell to their lowest level in more than three years Bloomberg.com [Feb 19]. The AI scare trade has also reached real estate Reuters [Feb 13], weighing on service-heavy and office landlords.

Reported: Few REIT prints landed in the window; the relevant signal is macro. The 10Y's 18 bps drop over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-19) has eased funding costs, but it has not yet produced the transaction recovery that residential and office owners need.

EPS Upside Watch: Data-centre and tower REITs remain the earnings-growth pocket, while lower mortgage rates should eventually lift transaction volumes and fee income for residential landlords and brokers.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Big Tech is buying up America's land and home builders can't compete WSJ [Feb 17]: hyperscaler land demand reprices land for everyone, a cost headwind for builders and a tailwind for land-rich owners.

Narrative: Utilities have become a growth sector: XLU rose 7.18% over 20 sessions to 46.11 and NextEra 9.29% to 91.64 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19), on the view that data-centre load growth turns rate-base expansion into compounding EPS.

Reported: Southern Co raised its spending plan by 7% as data-centre power demand swells Reuters [Feb 19]. Every capex upgrade expands the rate base on which regulated returns are earned, so plan raises translate into higher long-term EPS growth.

EPS Upside Watch: Independent power producers with merchant exposure lead: Vistra rose 7.71% and Constellation 5.35% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). Contract announcements with hyperscalers are the catalyst for estimate upgrades.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Affordability politics is the underrated risk: Pennsylvania's governor is telling data centres to 'pay for your own power' Politico [Feb 19]. If cost allocation shifts to hyperscalers, regulated utilities keep their growth but IPPs lose pricing power — favour wires-and-poles names over merchant generators.

Narrative: European autos remain in an earnings reset driven by tariffs, China and restructuring. The STOXX autos ETF (EXV5) is up just 0.02% over 20 sessions at 45.96, Stellantis is down 24.29% at 7.51 and Renault fell 3.10% in the prior session to 32.16 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19).

Reported: Mercedes' 2025 earnings more than halved on tariff costs and China woes Automotive News [Feb 12], the clearest read of how US tariffs hit German premium margins. BMW is the relative winner, up 2.46% over 20 sessions at 90.08 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19).

EPS Upside Watch: Self-help is the only lever: Volkswagen plans to cut costs by 20% by the end of 2028 Reuters [Feb 16]. Estimates can rise on cost delivery even if volumes stay flat, so VW and BMW screen better than Stellantis.

⚡ Breaking Convention: BMW's relative strength while Volkswagen preference shares fell 2.56% over 20 sessions to 102.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19) shows the sector is not one trade: a long BMW, short Stellantis pair isolates premium pricing from volume risk.

Narrative: Semis are bifurcating around a memory squeeze: AI is gobbling up memory chips and causing a critical shortage Bloomberg.com [Feb 16]. SOXX is up 2.21% over 20 sessions at 355.84, TSMC 10.51% and Micron 7.26%, while AMD fell 18.59% and Intel 17.75% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19).

Reported: Applied Materials gave a rosy forecast as AI and memory boost demand Bloomberg.com [Feb 13], confirming that the capex wave reaches equipment before end demand. ASML is up 7.27% over 20 sessions at 1,458.93 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19).

EPS Upside Watch: Memory pricing drives the biggest revisions: Micron, Samsung and SK Hynix benefit directly, and equipment makers follow as capacity is added. Nvidia's results on Feb. 25 The Motley Fool [Feb 17] are the sector's next estimate reset.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The squeeze has victims: rising memory costs pressure PC, phone and console makers, and the slides in AMD and Intel show the market already separating AI data-centre winners from consumer-exposed chips. Own memory and equipment; avoid the consumer-PC complex.

Rewarded: Companies that paired results with raised guidance, growth or capital returns: Deere jumped on a higher outlook WSJ [Feb 19], Occidental on a debt cut and dividend hike 24/7 Wall St. [Feb 19], DoorDash on a stronger growth forecast Reuters [Feb 19], and Applied Materials on an AI and memory-driven forecast Bloomberg.com [Feb 13].

Punished: Beats with soft guidance were sold: Walmart's cautious outlook overshadowed steady sales Reuters [Feb 19], EPAM plunged despite beating Barron's [Feb 19] and Medtronic fell on an unchanged outlook Reuters [Feb 17]. Tariff-hit results drew the harshest reactions, with Pinterest down nearly 17% CNBC [Feb 13], while Mercedes' earnings more than halved Automotive News [Feb 12].

Pattern: The market pays for forward visibility in the physical economy and in AI hardware, and discounts beats in services exposed to AI substitution or tariff-squeezed customers. Capital discipline — debt reduction, buybacks, dividends — is rewarded more than volume growth, consistent with energy and industrials leading.

Attention into EPS: Nvidia on Feb. 25 is the dominant event The Motley Fool [Feb 17]. With the stock up only 2.50% over 20 sessions at 187.90 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19), the bar is guidance on data-centre demand and supply, not the headline beat.

Playbook: Into reports, buy names where guidance risk is skewed up — equipment, memory, industrial capex — and sell beats in software and consumer platforms that lack guidance raises. Fade post-earnings pops that are not backed by higher full-year guidance, and treat a beat-and-hold as a sell signal in crowded defensives.

Attention Gap: Rare-earth prices surged above the floor price given to MP Materials Reuters [Feb 18], turning a policy backstop into a margin tailwind. The theme gets headlines around US–China talks but little allocation in broad portfolios, and a price floor changes the risk profile of the whole non-China supply chain.

Exposure & Risk: Express through MP Materials and Lynas, or the VanEck REMX basket for diversification. Risks: a US–China summit deal that eases export controls would deflate the scarcity premium, and with prices already above the floor, the floor offers no near-term downside protection.

Attention Gap: The crude glut is a boon for US refiners as fuel demand stays firm Bloomberg.com [Feb 11], yet attention is fixed on upstream producers and the Iran premium. Refiners earn the spread, so they win if crude stays abundant while geopolitics lifts product prices.

Exposure & Risk: Valero, Marathon Petroleum and Phillips 66, or the CRAK refiners ETF. Risk: a US strike on Iran that spikes crude faster than gasoline and diesel compresses margins, and a demand slowdown would hit cracks; size modestly and pair against long crude exposure.

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was 66,957.52, up 0.8% on the day but down 4.03% over five sessions and 20.41% over 20 sessions; ether closed at 1,948.20, down 27.91%, and Solana at 82.39, down 29.80% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). IBIT is down 25.51% over 20 sessions at 38.07 and MSTR 20.98% at 129.45, while Coinbase bounced 8.32% over five sessions to 165.94 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19).

New / Most Important: Bitcoin losing $70,000 is a warning sign for further downside, per CoinDesk CoinDesk [Feb 18], and spot bitcoin, ether and XRP ETFs are bleeding while Solana bucks the outflow trend CoinDesk [Feb 19]. With the marginal ETF buyer gone quiet, price is being set by sellers and hedgers rather than new allocations.

Playbook: Stay underweight crypto beta until bitcoin reclaims $70,000 on a daily close CoinDesk [Feb 18]; use rallies to buy downside protection rather than spot. A close above that level with ETF inflows returning would justify re-entering via IBIT. Prefer COIN over MSTR for any rebound, since Coinbase has already turned while MSTR carries leverage to the bitcoin price.

Rates & Dollar: The DXY rose 1.14% over five sessions to 97.93 but is down 0.84% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). Duration has worked: TLT gained 2.65% over 20 sessions to 89.62 as the 10Y fell 18 bps to 4.08% and the curve bull-flattened (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19; US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-19). Hawkish minutes The New York Times [Feb 18] explain the dollar's short-term bounce.

Credit Check: Public credit is calm — HYG is down only 0.22% over 20 sessions at 80.94 and LQD up 1.01% at 111.68 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). The cracks are in private, illiquid credit: Blue Owl halted redemptions at one of its funds Reuters [Feb 19], and that is where we expect the next spread widening to start.

Portfolio Implication: Keep a modest duration overweight through TLT or IEF as a hedge against an Iran or private-credit shock, prefer investment grade to high yield, and avoid semi-liquid private-credit vehicles. Hold some dollar exposure while the Fed is on hold; fade it if the 2Y breaks below its 3.47% close on a soft inflation print (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-19).

What Is Priced: Brent at 71.66 is up 9.84% over 20 sessions, gold front-month sits at 4,997.40 and the VIX at 20.23 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19): a partial risk premium. Iran says the US is risking a 'crisis' as Trump sets a '10, 15 days' deadline for a deal Al Jazeera [Feb 19].

Conditional Expression: If strikes come, oil could spike by as much as $15 a barrel Yahoo Finance [Feb 19]: own Brent call spreads and XLE, add defence, and short airlines and EUR/USD. If a deal is struck, the premium built over 20 sessions unwinds quickly, so rotate into airlines, discretionary and European cyclicals and take profits on energy.

Risk: Timing is binary and headline-driven, and a crude glut caps the upside if supply is not actually disrupted Bloomberg.com [Feb 11]. Express the view with options rather than futures, and keep position sizes small enough to survive a weekend gap.

What Is Priced: A Supreme Court ruling on the tariffs is pending CNBC [Feb 19], and importers, small caps and tariff-hit retailers trade as if the status quo holds: IWM is down 1.19% over 20 sessions at 264.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19).

Conditional Expression: If the tariffs are struck down, buy tariff-hit importers, small caps and equal-weight retail, and expect Treasuries to price lost revenue at the long end. If they are upheld, stay with domestic producers and keep importers underweight.

Risk: The administration can rebuild tariffs under other statutes, so any relief rally in importers may fade; position through short-dated options and watch the 10Y for a deficit reaction around its 4.08% close (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-19).

Catalyst & Thesis: Nvidia reports on Feb. 25 The Motley Fool [Feb 17]. Meta's multiyear deal to buy millions of Nvidia chips Reuters [Feb 17] locks in hyperscaler demand, so the debate is supply and margins, with the memory squeeze the main input cost to watch in the guide. We expect guidance, not the beat, to drive the move, and the setup is constructive after weeks of sideways trading.

Price Hurdle & Risk: NVDA closed at 187.90, up 2.50% over 20 sessions but down 1.13% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19). A guide that fails to lift data-centre expectations, or commentary that AI capex is peaking, would break the thesis; investor worry about the capex race is the main sentiment risk.

Catalyst & Thesis: Blue Owl unloaded $1.4 billion in assets WSJ [Feb 19] and halted redemptions at one of its funds, deepening the selloff in private-equity shares Reuters [Feb 19]. The business model depends on retail inflows into semi-liquid vehicles; until redemptions normalise, fee growth and multiples are at risk.

Price Hurdle & Risk: OWL is not on our price card; the hurdle for the short is a stabilisation in fund flows. Risk: banks such as Bank of America are committing their own cash to private credit Bloomberg.com [Feb 19], so well-bid loan sales could quickly reassure investors and squeeze shorts.

Catalyst & Thesis: Occidental jumped as a $5.8 billion debt cut and dividend hike impressed investors 24/7 Wall St. [Feb 19]. With Brent at 71.66 and the Iran deadline live (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19), lower leverage converts the oil premium into equity value faster than for more indebted peers.

Price Hurdle & Risk: OXY is not on our price card; use XLE, up 13.19% over 20 sessions at 55.18 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19), as the hurdle the stock must keep pace with. Risk: a US–Iran deal unwinds the oil premium and leaves the rerating resting on debt reduction alone.
Observed Attention: Raspberry Pi's chief executive embraced the meme-stock label after a 94% rally Bloomberg.com [Feb 19], an unusual endorsement that keeps the London-listed stock on retail screens.

Motivation & Bias: The hook is cheap exposure to edge-AI hardware while AI chip stocks feel crowded; the bias is momentum-chasing in a thinly traded mid-cap where management's embrace of the meme label adds fuel.
Instrument & Risk: Only small cash-equity positions with a hard stop; liquidity is thin and the rally has outrun any earnings revision. The risk is a sharp reversal once momentum stalls.
Observed Attention: Reddit traders are betting $80K on DHT as tanker rates hit record highs Yahoo Finance [Feb 19].

Motivation & Bias: Retail is chasing a cash-flow story — record day rates feed straight into a tanker owner's earnings — with the Iran confrontation adding a geopolitical kicker. The bias is assuming rates only go up.

Instrument & Risk: DHT shares or a basket of crude tanker owners, sized small; a US–Iran deal or a slowdown in crude exports would cool rates quickly, and spot-exposed tankers fall as fast as they rise.

Observed Attention: Barron's describes Tesla as a retail investor favourite that is under pressure Barron's [Feb 19]; TSLA closed at 411.71, down 4.57% over 20 sessions and 3.87% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19).
Motivation & Bias: Retail buys the autonomy and AI narrative and the dip in a familiar name, while institutions focus on auto fundamentals; the bias is loyalty and anchoring to past highs.

Instrument & Risk: Use defined-risk call spreads rather than leveraged ETFs. The risk is that auto fundamentals, not narrative, set the next leg, and XLY's 4.25% slide over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19) shows the sector backdrop is not helping.
Observed Attention: Robinhood's $1 billion fund pitches pre-IPO stock as the next craze Bloomberg.com [Feb 17], opening private markets to retail accounts.

Motivation & Bias: Retail wants the private names it cannot buy before IPO, and Robinhood monetises that demand; the bias is ignoring illiquidity — the same mismatch that forced Blue Owl to halt redemptions at one of its funds Reuters [Feb 19].

Instrument & Risk: HOOD is a levered bet on retail activity; with bitcoin down 20.41% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-19), crypto trading revenue is at risk, so prefer call spreads to stock and cut if crypto weakness deepens.
